scope.question: Does a predeclared earlier validation-loss checkpoint-selection rule generalize better than a fixed update-2688 endpoint when both checkpoints come from the same fresh-seed training run?
scope.primaryHypothesis: The earlier-selected checkpoint is materially better than the same-run update-2688 control, by more than 0.02 paired-score points, against handcrafted evaluation.
scope.nullHypothesis: The earlier-selected checkpoint is not materially better than the same-run update-2688 control; its paired-score difference is at most +0.02 points.
doesNotTest: a causal separation of corpus, initialization, recipe, or session effects
a universal claim that update 768 is the correct endpoint
scope.decisionBoundary: This contract can produce development evidence for checkpoint selection only. It cannot reopen the failed Step 9 confirmation or authorize a model change.
scope.uncertaintyBoundary: The primary interval is conditional on this one fresh training run and its fixed opening source. It does not estimate seed variance, selection-rule variance, corpus variance, or session/thermal variance.

priorEvidence.interpretation: The observed u768 result motivates a prospective selection-rule test. It is not evidence that later training caused overfitting, and the exposed diagnosis cells cannot validate a general rule by themselves.

historicalTrainer.use: provenance and recipe reference only; this wrapper hardcodes the historical Model B identity and cannot launch Step 10

requiredProperties: does not hardcode Model B's historical seed or experiment ID
binds experimentId, fresh seed, frozen corpus, and every candidate checkpoint
records the 4,096-update learning-rate schedule horizon while stopping at update 2,688
records validation at every 128 updates and fails closed on any missing candidate
binds trainer, serializer, and runtime identities before launch

invariants.omittedSettings: Every optimizer and loader field not restated here is inherited from the hash-bound historical Model B recipe; no library default may silently fill an omitted setting.

exposure.positionAndExposureCoupling: The early candidate cap and update-2688 control are different exposure points in one schedule; this coupling is reported, not treated as isolated causality.

selectionRule.name: lowest-validation-loss-within-early-cap-v1
selectionRule.metric: finite validation teacher-only loss on the frozen 60,000-record validation binary
selectionRule.selection: Let globalMinimum be the lowest finite validation loss across all eight predeclared candidate updates. Select the earliest candidate whose loss is within 1e-12 of globalMinimum.

control.selection: fixed before training and never replaced by a game result or validation result

eligibility: all eight predeclared candidate updates must be present
validation has the exact frozen record count and order
training and validation diagnostics are complete
full-precision export, integer reference, native, and WASM parity pass before any match
selectionRule.missingOrInvalidCandidatePolicy: A missing checkpoint, missing validation receipt, nonfinite loss, incomplete diagnostic, export failure, or qualification failure for any of the eight candidate updates stops the experiment before matches; the candidate set may not be silently reduced.
selectionRule.interpretation: The rule is tested prospectively on one new seed and one frozen corpus. A selected early checkpoint is evidence about this rule under this exposure, not proof of a universal update endpoint or proof of overtraining.

corpusFamilyExclusion.familyDefinition: canonical color-swap board family using the repository's packed-board reader, matching the generator's canonical_family implementation
corpusFamilyExclusion.check: Every generated opening's canonical family, including its color swap, must be absent from every listed corpus artifact. The check must run before the opening suite is frozen and must fail closed.

openingProtocol.abandonedPartialPolicy: Do not inspect, hash, read, or pass the abandoned 1,000 ms partial path to the generator. Its outcomes remain unopened and excluded by policy.
openingProtocol.preMatchBinding: The future execution contract must bind the generated output, generator build, independent validation receipt, and corpus-family exclusion receipt. No training outcome or model score may influence generation, filtering, ranking, or suite size.

matchProtocol.endpoint: 1,000 ms per move native production-search development endpoint

requirements: caffeinate tied only to owned runner

models.label: early-selected
models.network: the checkpoint selected by selectionRule from this run

models.label: u2688-control
models.network: the update-2688 export from this same run

schedule.openingMapping: Block b contains generated opening rows [32*b, 32*(b+1)) in original order; both cells use the identical mapping and each pair runs candidate colors in both seats.

searchSettings.depthCapMeaning: No explicit depth cap or node cap is passed; both engines use the exact frozen production-search defaults under the fixed movetime.

requirements: automatic strict validation after every block
validates both cells and exact command bindings
recomputes WDL and pair scores from raw games
rejects missing, duplicate, malformed, fallback, or failed games
does not open scores before both cells pass

matchProtocol.scoreDisclosure: Expose only pass/fail, completion counts, active block, failures, and timing until both complete cells validate.

incompletePolicy.processInterruption: Send Ctrl+C once to the owned process, wait briefly, then SIGTERM only that owned process if required. Preserve and exclude the incomplete attempt; rerun the complete block under a new attempt only if budget remains.
incompletePolicy.correctnessFailure: Stop the experiment immediately; do not auto-retry a correctness failure.
incompletePolicy.repeatedFailure: A second failure from the same cause stops the experiment and is reported.

pairScore.definition: For one opening pair, pairScore is the arithmetic mean of the two color-swapped game scores. The primary contrast is the mean of per-opening pair-score differences.

statistics.primaryContrast: mean pair score of early-selected minus mean pair score of u2688-control on the same opening IDs, both against handcrafted

decision.success: two-sided 95% interval lower endpoint is greater than +0.02
decision.failure: two-sided 95% interval upper endpoint is less than -0.02, which is evidence of material inferiority of the early-selected checkpoint; failure to meet success is not by itself failure
decision.inconclusive: all other intervals, including intervals that do not establish a material improvement or material inferiority
decision.claimType: exploratory development evidence only; no confirmatory or deployment claim

secondaryReporting: each model's WDL and paired score versus handcrafted
validation-loss-selected update and all candidate losses
training exposure, learning rate, and checkpoint provenance
statistics.multiplicity: Only the predeclared early-selected-minus-u2688 contrast is the primary decision. Secondary model-versus-handcrafted values are descriptive and do not alter selection or stopping.
statistics.conditionalInterpretation: The interval quantifies opening uncertainty conditional on the one fresh run and fixed suite; it excludes variability in seeds, corpora, selection rules, and sessions.

beforeTraining: verify all corpus, trainer, serializer, plan, and base-recipe hashes
bind and validate a separate Step 10 runner and resolved configuration
run the real CPU trainer fixture and exact resume/export checks
prove validation at every 128-update candidate and explicit update-2688 export
confirm the fresh seed is not reused from A or B
record a fresh throughput, storage, and cost forecast; a quote is nonbinding until explicit approval
beforeMatches: bind the generated development suite and receipt
verify selected checkpoint rule from validation-only data
verify u2688 control comes from the same run
measure full-precision-to-integer quantization error separately without requiring it to be zero
verify exact runtime, command, suite, model, and seed bindings
run rejection fixtures for missing/duplicate pairs, wrong network/suite/settings, malformed WDL, and fallback/failure states
stopImmediately: missing or invalid candidate checkpoint or validation receipt
illegal move, fallback, missing result, or malformed termination
opening overlap or invalid generation receipt
parityAndPreflight.recoverableInterruption: Only an owned process interruption may use the bounded rerun policy in matchProtocol.incompletePolicy. It does not authorize retry after a correctness failure.
parityAndPreflight.candidateSetFailure: Any missing or invalid candidate stops before matches; no candidate is silently dropped.

mustInclude: measured throughput probe or justified historical transfer
training and export wall-time forecast through update 2688
peak storage including checkpoints and logs
fresh GPU quote if rental is proposed
MBP match wall-time forecast for 512 games

budget.quotePolicy: Historical quotes are nonbinding. A fresh quote and explicit user approval are required before any rental or training.
budget.budgetStop: stop and report; never label a budget stop as convergence or strength failure

output.outcomeSeal: Do not open WDL, scores, pair scores, or outcome-bearing game records until both complete cells pass validation.

neverDo: rent GPU or start training from this draft
run opening generation before independent review
run matches before opening and artifact bindings are complete
use Step 9 confirmation or diagnosis outcomes to alter the rule
exclusions.authorizationRule: Review, artifact binding, and a valid contract do not authorize opening generation, training, matches, or GPU rental. Each corresponding authorization flag requires separate explicit user authorization.

requiredAmendments: bind a separate executable Step 10 runner and config; retain the historical B wrapper as provenance only
fail closed on any missing or invalid candidate and define global-minimum tie handling
correct the opening generator binary, expand exclusions, and add generator/build, corpus-family, and independent validation receipts
freeze exact match blocks, seeds, command settings, runner/analyzer hashes, and interruption policy
define pair-score averaging and distinguish material inferiority from failure to show improvement
state that review and artifact binding alone authorize no compute and require a prelaunch budget forecast
reviewMustCheck: selection rule is fully predeclared and not fitted to match outcomes
same-run control makes the primary comparison interpretable
corpus and seed coupling/confounds are explicitly disclosed
opening provenance and exclusion gate is adequate
no authorization or confirmation boundary is accidentally widened
